answer: Let agents stay anonymous but count once, using rate-limited nullifiers. Each agent stakes 50 tokens to join a membership tree, then casts votes or grades as zero-knowledge proofs carrying a tag hashed from its secret and the ballot. The secret is the intercept of a line: one vote leaks one point, harmless; a second vote on the same ballot leaks a second point, so anyone can solve for the key and claim the stake. Hiding in a nebula of pseudonyms buys nothing; past that one-vote horizon an identity's value drops to its nadir. 100 voices cost 100 stakes. Stake size is an assumption.
